extracted.intended_audience: AI/ML researchers, legal informatics scholars, legal-tech developers, and policymakers interested in LLM evaluation for legal tasks
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and running retrieval-augmented evaluations of large language models on synthetic multiple-choice tax-law questions (CFR and U.S. Code), varying retrieval methods, prompting techniques, and model choice to measure legal reasoning and accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthetic multiple-choice problem generation to avoid data contamination
rubrics_metrics.description: We generate multiple-choice problems, each consisting of a question and a set of potential answers (only one of which is correct). The facts, names and numbers for each problem are randomly generated by Python code. As a result, our synthetic validation set consists solely of brand-new problems that do not exist on the internet and could not have been included in the training set for any LLM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each generated problem contains: (1) the legal question with answer options for the LLM to choose from; (2) the correct option; (3) the explanation for why that option is correct; and (4) the citation to the specific part of the law in which the answer to the question can be determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy measured by selecting the correct multiple-choice option
rubrics_metrics.description: For each question, we prompt an LLM to pick one of the multiple-choice answers, and we evaluate the LLM’s performance based on whether it chooses the correct answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because models don’t always produce outputs in a consistent format, the authors utilise GPT-4 to compare the ground truth to the outputted answer for large-scale grading (see separate rubric for grader validation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of GPT-4 as an automated grader (LLM grader) and grader validation
rubrics_metrics.description: We utilise the most powerful available LLM, GPT-4, to compare the ground truth to the outputted answer. GPT-4 is instructed to grade the accuracy of a predicted answer choice by comparing it to the real answer choice for a given question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before deploying this evaluation method at scale, the authors validated it on a subset: GPT-4 'perfectly graded nearly all of these questions,' erring less than ~1% of the time on ambiguous/difficult outputs from older models; manual review was used to check problematic cases (e.g., davinci producing multiple conflicting answer choices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrieval method: bypass_retrieval
rubrics_metrics.description: "bypass_retrieval" creates a baseline by providing the LLM with a multiple-choice question and the answer options with no additional explicitly provided legal context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses the ability of an LLM to answer a tax law question solely from its 'internal knowledge base' (i.e., without retrieval augmentation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrieval method: similarity_search
rubrics_metrics.description: "similarity_search" injects potentially relevant legal text into the prompt by retrieving documents from a vector database using embeddings and cosine similarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offline, statutes and regulations are extracted into discrete subsection documents (CFR ~130 tokens average; U.S. Code ~250 tokens average). The system retrieves the four most 'relevant' documents by cosine similarity (using GTR-large embeddings) and injects them as context; the LLM is instructed to return metadata for referenced subsections. Note: GTR-large was trained on non-legal text, so this is an 'out-of-domain' embedding use-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrieval method: gold_truth
rubrics_metrics.description: "gold_truth" provides, as context, the correct source material for the question by referencing the question's citation to the specific part of law it pertains to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to estimate the impact of theoretically best possible retrieval and to isolate errors caused by inaccurate retrieval in similarity_search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrieval method: lecture_notes
rubrics_metrics.description: "lecture_notes" supplies context to the LLM in the form of lecture notes (written by an expert co-author) relevant to the given question type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides domain-expert explanatory context rather than verbatim statute text; compares effectiveness of pedagogical notes versus statutory/regulatory texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompting technique: chain-of-thought (CoT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chain-of-thought prompting asks the LLM to think through its response step-by-step (i.e., 'Let's think step by step').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CoT does not consistently improve results for all models/methods, but it boosts performance of higher-capability models (notably GPT-4). The paper notes that an LLM may need a certain capability level to exhibit improvement via CoT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompting technique: few-shot prompting
rubrics_metrics.description: Few-shot prompting provides the LLM with a set of three other question-answer pair examples (matching the question type) along with the question being asked to guide how to answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied without providing contextual source documents or lecture notes; strongly improves GPT-4 performance and is less consistently useful for weaker models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mega_run (upper-bound combined setting)
rubrics_metrics.description: "mega_run" combines the 'gold_truth' retrieval method, few-shot prompting, and CoT prompting of GPT-4 to assess the upper bound on performance with these techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to estimate the best achievable accuracy with current techniques and the most powerful model and to visualise maximum gains from combined methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary experimental factor: underlying LLM capability/model choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Which underlying LLM is used is a primary factor causing consistent increases in accuracy; experiments run across 'davinci', 'text-davinci-002', 'gpt-3.5-turbo', and 'gpt-4'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newer, larger, more-capable models outperform older models. This factor dominates average accuracy improvements across other factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deterministic generation via temperature=0
rubrics_metrics.description: For all models across experiments, temperature was set equal to zero when generating responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower temperatures make outputs more deterministic; used to reduce variance attributable to sampling randomness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context-window and truncation constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Models have finite context windows (davinci 2049 tokens; text-davinci-002 and gpt-3.5-turbo 4097 tokens; gpt-4 8192 tokens), and when supplying supporting context to models with smaller context windows, retrieved context was sometimes truncated to fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The effective amount of context provided (and truncation strategy) may affect model performance; prompt length and optimal use of context are suggested areas for future analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding choice and vector-database design for retrieval
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors used GTR-large to compute 768-dimensional embeddings for discrete subsection documents and FAISS-like similarity search (Facebook AI Similarity Search) with cosine similarity to retrieve top documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Average subsection token lengths reported (CFR ~130 tokens, U.S. Code ~250 tokens); authors note embeddings were out-of-domain for legal text and that retrieval hyperparameters (embedding model, subsection size, number retrieved) materially affect retrieval quality and thereby accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation task composition: CFR and U.S. Code exams and question subtypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Two overarching multiple-choice exams were generated: one based on the CFR and one on the U.S. Code. The CFR and U.S. Code exams are composed of three and four sections, respectively, with each 100-question section pertaining to a specific tax law question type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFR question types: (1) 'Check the Box' (entity status), (2) 'Restricted Property as Compensation/Employee', (3) 'Part Gift/Part Sale'. U.S. Code question types: (1) 'Restricted Property as Compensation/Employer', (2) 'Unrestricted Property as Compensation', (3) basis-related group ('Basis of Property Transferred as Gift', 'Basis of Property Transferred at Death', 'Basis from Part Donation/Part Sale'), (4) 'Qualified Business Income Deduction (Section 199A)'. These task types probe different reasoning and arithmetic demands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measuring effect of legal-context relevance/amount on accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: One experiment dimension measures whether giving the LLM more legal text and more relevant legal text increases accuracy (moving from bypass_retrieval to gold_truth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results show a weak but observable improvement as more/relevant legal source material is provided; this dimension helps quantify sensitivity to contextual grounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt-template per retrieval method and instruction style
rubrics_metrics.description: Each retrieval method had its own prompt template that provides different supporting context to the LLM (Appendix contains full prompt template examples, e.g., the GPT-4 'mega_run' prompt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt engineering choices (instructions like 'If you don't know the answer, just say "I don't know the answer." Don't make up an answer.' and inclusion of examples) are part of the evaluation design and affect outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual review for ambiguous or malformed model outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Older/weaker models occasionally produce outputs with multiple conflicting answer choices or inconsistent formatting that can mislead automated graders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors manually reviewed much of the davinci grading to verify automated grading trends and to ensure rare grader errors did not materially affect overall reported trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate retrieval-improvement levers as next-step evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Future evaluation should vary and optimise retrieval-related hyperparameters (choice of embeddings model, retrieval technique, token length of vector database subsections, and number of subsections retrieved) to close the gap between similarity_search and gold_truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper identifies these factors as critical experimental knobs that influence the quality of grounding documents and therefore model legal-reasoning accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of domain-expert pedagogical context as an alternative augmentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing lecture notes (domain-expert pedagogical context) is treated as a distinct augmentation method (lecture_notes) to compare against statutory/regulatory grounding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This probes whether explanations/teaching-style context can substitute or complement direct legal text to improve LLM performance.
